record.paper_title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
record.original_question: Let n=4k+1 for an integer k≥1, let S be a k-element subset of {1,2,...,2k}, and let the extended Petersen graph XP(2n,S) have vertex set Z_n×{1,2}, edges within the first layer determined by circular distances in S, edges within the second layer determined by the complementary set of distances, and matching edges joining the two copies of each x in Z_n. Apart from the Petersen graph itself, is every extended Petersen graph Class 1, meaning edge-colorable with Δ(G) colors?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1 (Horák, Rosa [1]) Every extended Petersen graph, except Petersen graph itself, is of Class 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer k ≥ 1 and let n = 4k+1. For a k-element subset S ⊆ {1, 2, …, 2k}, define the extended Petersen graph XP(2n, S) as follows. Its vertex set is Z_n × {1, 2}. Edges are of three types:
(i) "Inner" edges within layer 1: vertices (x, 1) and (y, 1) are adjacent whenever the circular distance min(|x − y|, n − |x − y|) belongs to S.
(ii) "Outer" edges within layer 2: vertices (x, 2) and (y, 2) are adjacent whenever the circular distance min(|x − y|, n − |x − y|) belongs to {1, 2, …, 2k} \ S.
(iii) "Spoke" edges joining (x, 1) and (x, 2) for every x ∈ Z_n.
Recall that a graph G is Class 1 if its edge chromatic index χ′(G) equals its maximum degree Δ(G), and Class 2 otherwise.

Prove or disprove: with the sole exception of the Petersen graph itself, every extended Petersen graph XP(2n, S) (for n = 4k+1, k ≥ 1, S a k-subset of {1, …, 2k}) is Class 1.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a published resolution of the Horák–Rosa conjecture that every extended Petersen graph other than the Petersen graph is Class 1; the conjecture is restated as an open problem in the recent workshop problem collection. No proof or counterexample appears in the indexed literature.
